source_text:
Ἔγνων δὲ παροδεύσαντάς τινας ἐκεῖθεν, ἔχοντας κακὴν διδαχήν: οὓς οὐκ εἰάσατε σπεῖραι εἰς ὑμᾶς, βύσαντες τὰ ὦτα, εἰς τὸ μὴ παραδέξασθαι τὰ σπειρόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν, ὡς ὄντες λίθοι ναοῦ πατρός, ἡτοιμασμένοι εἰς οἰκοδομὴν θεοῦ πατρός, ἀναφερόμενοι εἰς τὰ ὕψη διὰ τῆς μηχανῆς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν σταυρός, σχοινίῳ χρώμενοι τῷ πνεύματι τῷ ἁγίῳ: ἡ δὲ πίστις ὑμῶν ἀναγωγεὺς ὑμῶν, ἡ δὲ ἀγάπη ὁδὸς ἡ ἀναφέρουσα εἰς θεόν.
ἐστὲ οὖν καὶ σύνοδοι πάντες, θεοφόροι καὶ ναοφόροι, χριστοφόροι, ἁγιοφόροι, κατὰ πάντα κεκοσμημένοι ἐντολαῖς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: οἶς καὶ ἀγαλλιώμενος ἠξιώθην δἰ ὦν γράφω προσομιλῆσαι ὑμῖν καὶ συγχαρῆναι, ὅτι κατ’ ἀνθρώπων βίον οὐδὲν ἀγαπᾶτε εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν.
thought_title: The Ephesians as stones of the Father's temple
orientation: Ignatius is praising the Ephesian church for refusing to let false teachers sow their bad teaching among them, and he is describing their spiritual state as stones being lifted up to God.
pass_a_gloss: But I learned that some people passed through from there, having bad teaching: whom you did not allow to sow into you, having plugged your ears, so as not to receive the things sown by them, as being stones of the temple of the Father, prepared for the building of God the Father, being carried up to the heights through the crane of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, using as a rope the Holy Spirit: and your faith is your hoist, and love is the way that carries up to God. Therefore you are all also fellow-travelers, god-bearers and temple-bearers, Christ-bearers, holy-thing-bearers, adorned in all things with the commandments of Jesus Christ: in whom also rejoicing I was deemed worthy through what I write to converse with you and to rejoice together, because according to the life of humans you love nothing except only God.

choices.why: The word means a mechanical device or engine for lifting; keeping 'machine' preserves the concrete image of a construction crane or hoist that Ignatius is building.
This rare word denotes something that lifts or carries upward; 'hoist' matches the construction imagery of the passage.
The word means companions on a journey; 'fellow-travelers' keeps the sense of shared movement toward God.
The compound means bearers of holy things; the literal rendering preserves the parallel with the other -φόροι compounds.

choices.english: according to the life of humans
choices.why: The phrase contrasts human standards of love with love for God alone; the literal rendering keeps the contrast explicit.

pass_b_english: I have learned that certain people passed through from there carrying evil teaching, and you did not let them sow it among you. You plugged your ears so as not to receive what they were sowing, since you are stones of the Father's temple, prepared for the building of God the Father. You are being lifted up to the heights by the crane of Jesus Christ, which is the cross, with the Holy Spirit as the rope. Your faith is the crane that lifts you, and love is the road that carries you up to God.

So you are all fellow travelers, bearers of God and bearers of the temple, bearers of Christ, bearers of holy things, adorned in every way with the commandments of Jesus Christ. And I rejoice in these things, since I have been counted worthy through what I write to speak with you and to rejoice with you, because according to the life of humans you love nothing except God alone.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'council of elders' for πρεσβυτέριον, but σύνοδοι here means 'companions/assemblies', not the technical term. However, 'fellow-travelers' misses that σύνοδοι here means gathered assemblies/companions in a church context; but more critically, the glossary term 'council of elders' is not at issue here. Actually: σύνοδοι is not in the glossary. But 'fellow-travelers' is an unusual rendering. Let me re-check: the word is σύνοδοι (plural), from σύνοδος, meaning 'assembly, company, companions.' 'Fellow-travelers' is a possible but strained rendering. However, this is not a glossary violation. Let me re-examine more carefully.
last_rejected.ruling: No glossary violation; σύνοδοι not in glossary. 'Fellow-travelers' is within σύνοδος range (traveling companions).

last_rejected.why: σύνοδοι means assemblies/companions, not fellow-travelers (which suggests political sympathizers).
last_rejected.ruling: σύνοδος can mean traveling companions; 'fellow-travelers' fits the journey metaphor (ἀναγωγεύς, ὁδός) here.

last_rejected.quote: you love nothing except God alone
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲν ἀγαπᾶτε εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν
last_rejected.why: The English omits 'alone' (μόνον), weakening the exclusivity: 'nothing except only God.'
last_rejected.fix: you love nothing except God alone
last_rejected.ruling: 'except God alone' renders εἰ μὴ μόνον τὸν θεόν; 'except...alone' preserves μόνον adequately.
